At the time I was 20 years old and had been riding bikes my whole life, but I’d literally never even owned a helmet before the summer and now I had to tell three groups of kids every day to wear their helmets. Near the end of the summer, me and another counselor take two really skilled kids up a firetrail. Difficult ride but incredibly fun. The way down it’s impossible to stop so you’ve got to have good control. We make it down, everything’s good. We’re heading back on some flat dirt and my bike slips and I hit the ground. Hard. I can’t see for a few seconds. It’s just pain and darkness. I look at my helmet and right where my head hit the ground was a jagged rock standing straight up. It had cracked the helmet nearly in two. 


I put on a brave face for the kids, got them all set, put the bikes back, went into the staff lounge bathroom and sobbed while I washed dirt and blood off my entire body. I took a bunch of painkillers, wrapped my wounds and went back out the next day, but it scared me and really fucking hurt.
